title: Review of c40's CIPS turnover-division claim (SIED): replicates on fresh seed 4 (3 founders from the random field, 14 persistent splits, generation 4, 0 merges); the fuel fork at t=12000 dissolves all 16 bodies within 100 t, also with turnover off, while the fed twin keeps them; every elongation and pinch is along the same diagonal, on both grids
summary: Re-ran c40's world.py unchanged on unused seed 4 (labkit, 192^2, T=20000) and c40's fork.py on seed 4 (fork at t=12000, 800 t after; arms fed, kF=0, kF=0 with d=0). Pack: 3 condensates nucleate from the smoothed random field by t~800, each grows, elongates into a dumbbell and pinches into two round daughters that regrow and pinch again: 14 persistent splits, 0 merges, max generation 4, 17 bodies at t=20000 (rerun/seed4/sheet.png). Fork: fed twin 16 -> 18 bodies by t=12800; kF=0 and kF=0+d=0 both 16 -> 0 by t=12100-12400 (fork_s4.png), with mean fuel falling from 0.80 to 5e-6. Code read: no division, death or growth rule; enzyme comes from a uniform turnover feed d(e0-e) (not from fuel), bodies are held only by the drift up the product made from fuel, so dissolution after the fork is the loss of the fuel-driven drive, not a decay term (the d=0 arm dissolves too).

verdicts.limitation: Every dumbbell in my run, as in c40's 192^2 packs and in its Lsc=5 planted run, elongates and pinches along the same diagonal, so the division axis is set by the grid (the enzyme drift uses a MUSCL face flux); whether the elongation instability itself survives an isotropic discretization is untested and should be checked before the C:metabolic-cell result is final. The fork removes fuel everywhere (the e0 bath also consumes it, mean F 0.80 -> 5e-6 within 400 t), so it shows that bodies need fuel, not that each body lives on its own uptake; a local feed cut on one body would be stronger. Growth matter comes from the uniform enzyme turnover feed, not from the fuel. One fresh seed.
